definition: Temperature is a setting that controls how adventurous the AI is when choosing its next word. Turn it down and you get the safest, most likely answer every time. Turn it up and the model takes more chances — more creative, more surprising, and more likely to go off the rails.

edges.label: shapes the odds
edges.note: Temperature rescales the probability distribution the next token is drawn from.

edges.label: high settings invite
edges.note: More randomness means more chances to drift from the facts.

example.body: Ask 'name our new dog-walking app' at high temperature and you get 'Wag Atlas,' 'Pawseidon,' 'Leash & Thank You.' Ask it to summarize a lease at high temperature and it might invent clauses that aren't there. Same model, different dial — creativity when you want it, chaos when you don't.
example.title: Two temperatures, one question

footnotes.body: Temperature rescales the softmax distribution over next-token probabilities before sampling: 0 makes output nearly deterministic (always the top token), 1.0 is the model's natural distribution, higher values flatten it toward uniform randomness. Often paired with top-p (nucleus) sampling, which truncates the tail of unlikely tokens.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: Temperature
tagline: The dial between predictable and creative in the AI's word choices.
whyItMatters: Temperature is the difference between a reliable tool and a brainstorming partner. Low for contracts, code, and summaries; higher for naming, ideas, and fiction. And when an AI gives you a noticeably different answer every time you ask the same question, temperature is usually why.
